## 固定收益市場主線

AI類股回升帶動短天期美債殖利率上揚，長天期公債則在聯準會決策前守穩，殖利率曲線因而趨平。2年期殖利率上升3.41個基點至4.7159%，10年期微降0.61個基點至4.9884%，30年期下降1.93個基點至5.3028%。美國經濟活動數據優於預期，配合長短端走勢分歧，顯示市場主要在重估對政策敏感的年期，而非全面撤出公債。

巴西的調整猛烈得多。總統魯拉意外連任，打亂投資人原先押注新政府將加強財政撙節的部位。部分較長天期利率交換上升逾300個基點，雷亞爾一度貶值11%，美元債表現落後其他新興市場。法國則反向走強：穆迪維持評等，使市場暫獲喘息，10年期公債相對德國的利差收窄14個基點。

AI融資為全球信用市場帶來另一項變化。SpaceX證實與Apollo簽訂約$400億的設備融資租賃，但仍待定價及交割；Meta尋求最高$950億股權資金，Anthropic則申請首次公開發行股票（IPO），同時揭露營收快速成長與持續的融資需求。這些消息帶動科技股回升，但債權人仍須面對同一問題：大規模建設有多少能靠營運現金支應，其餘資金又須付出何種融資條件。

## 經濟活動持穩，美債殖利率曲線趨平

週一美債調整集中在短端。5年期殖利率上升1.95個基點至4.8262%，與2年期同步遭到賣壓，10年期及30年期債券則上漲。2年與10年期利差收窄4.02個基點至27.25個基點，2年與30年期利差縮小5.34個基點至58.69個基點。長期借款成本仍高，但在股市情緒改善之際，長債比更直接受到近期政策決策影響的天期更能守穩。

拉長比較期間，長天期債券的表現仍較佳。10年期殖利率較一週前下降15.13個基點，較一個月前下降17.46個基點；30年期分別下降16.45與19.12個基點。2年期一週僅下降5.6個基點，月降幅則為13.81個基點。週一短端吐回部分近期漲幅，同時延續全週曲線趨平的走勢。

10年期名目殖利率微降，來自實質殖利率與通膨補償的小幅下滑：實質殖利率下降0.36個基點至2.6379%，損益兩平通膨率下降0.25個基點至2.3505%。過去一週，實質殖利率下降14.51個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.62個基點；過去一個月，實質殖利率下降18.61個基點，通膨補償反而上升1.15個基點。持續且較大幅的變動仍是實質殖利率下降，長期通膨補償並未明顯退卻。

新公布的數據顯示，美國經濟活動更為穩健。9月芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數由修正後的-0.08升至0.07，優於預估的-0.1；10月達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數由9.8升至13.4，也高於預估的7。全國性指標與區域製造業各自改善，與投資人在科技股修正期間所擔憂的成長轉弱情況不同。

美國財政部2年期公債標售得標殖利率為4.708%，低於前次的4.787%。週一次級市場2年期殖利率雖然上升，政府本次短天期新融資成本仍低於前次標售。

股市反彈幅度比債市變動更明顯。標普500指數上漲0.70%至7,676.77，那斯達克100指數上漲1.09%，費城半導體指數上漲2.82%；VIX下跌5.45%至18.39。不過，半導體股過去一個月仍下跌12.51%，那斯達克100指數也下跌4.36%。市場先前大幅重估AI融資與支出，當日價格雖改善，近期科技股趨勢仍明顯疲弱。

Treasury Partners的Richard Saperstein預期聯準會將維持利率，因為債市自9月以來已收緊信用條件。Principal Asset Management的Seema Shah同樣認為，決策官員主要是在回應能源通膨與匯率變化，而非經濟明顯過熱；她預期12月升息，2027年再升一次。經濟活動數據轉強，使兩者的區別更具意義：市場本身的緊縮效果可以支持政策耐心，不必以當期產出大幅下滑為前提。

能源仍帶來通膨風險，但當日油價回落。WTI原油期貨下跌1.46%至每桶$101.76，布蘭特原油期貨下跌0.78%至每桶$115.81。根據伊朗國營IRIB報導，伊朗總統裴澤斯基安在德黑蘭與沙烏地阿拉伯、巴基斯坦及土耳其安全官員會談時，呼籲深化區域合作並化解歧見。美國總統川普週末表示，即將決定達成協議或恢復攻擊；各國官員此行旨在重啟外交。油價回落減輕當日市場的一項壓力，外交結果仍未明朗。

黃金期貨上漲0.76%至每盎司$4,038.40。

美元指數上漲0.20%至102.017。信用市場方面，美國整體高收益債利差小幅收窄，與新興市場硬通貨債利差明顯擴大形成對比。投資等級債基金LQD報酬約0.15%，高收益債基金HYG約0.17%，新興市場債基金EMB則下跌約0.17%。這樣的分歧，呼應美國科技股回升與拉丁美洲重大主權衝擊同時出現的交易日。

## 巴西大選迫使市場重估財政風險

巴西選舉法院公布，魯拉在總統決選取得51.8%選票，擊敗得票48.2%的Flávio Bolsonaro。Bolsonaro首輪領先，使投資人普遍預期他將勝選，並帶來支出削減與利率下降，市場部位也大致朝此方向布局。魯拉反而獲得第四個任期，迫使投資人迅速重估下屆政府可能採取的財政調整。

既有部位放大了市場反應。Ibovespa指數開盤即下跌10%，隨即觸發2020年初以來首次熔斷，之後跌幅一度達17%；雷亞爾一度貶值11%，創逾20年最大跌幅。部分較長天期交換合約觸及交易限幅後，上升逾300個基點。交易所營運商B3擴大週一正常交易時段的匯率、利率與股價指數期貨限幅。

巴西財政部宣布標售買回本幣固定利率債券後，交換利率略為回穩，但各年期美元債仍下跌，部分價格跌逾2.6美分，表現落後其他新興市場主權債。對國內利率特別敏感的小型股，其基準指數下跌30%；一檔在美國掛牌的巴西股票基金盤中一度下跌26%。選後衝擊同時落在匯率、國內折現率與外債信用，而非僅限股市。

財政疑慮在於調整的規模與方式。巴西名目赤字超過GDP的9%，公共債務高於80%，法定強制支出又使預算彈性有限。魯拉強調維持社會福利、透過信用支持消費，公共財政修復主要仰賴增加收入。他競選期間承諾減免微型創業者債務、提前發放福利，也加深市場對支出抑制速度的疑慮。

魯拉表示，希望在下屆任期結束前，將不含利息支出的初級盈餘提高至GDP的1.5%。Bloomberg訪問的投資人認為仍不夠，因為高利息成本持續占用大量預算，修復規模更大的整體赤字仍有難度。Vanguard的Ales Koutny預期，持續的財政支出、更多公共投資與更長時間的高通膨，將限制降息空間，實質利率也須維持高檔。

融資影響已超出次級市場。Bloomberg報導，原排定選後進行的約$60億股票發行陷入不確定，這些交易原以Bolsonaro勝選為前提籌備。在借款昂貴、家庭拖欠率創紀錄並已拖累經濟之際，資產價格下跌也影響企業取得新資本的前景。

摩根大通將巴西匯率與利率部位評估由加碼降至市場權重，Bradesco BBI將股市展望降為中立。Bank of Nassau 1982的Win Thin認為，劇烈波動部分來自部位調整，也可能超跌，但魯拉的競選支出承諾確實惡化了基本面。富國銀行的Alvaro Vivanco則認為即時反應過度，預期政府初期將提出足夠財政措施控制風險，尤其能穩定匯率；他預期魯拉執政下，雷亞爾將升向每美元5.30。

下任財政部長人選將左右哪種看法獲得支持。政府官員表示，討論中的人選包括副總統Geraldo Alckmin與皮奧伊州州長Rafael Fonteles。市場對中間派資深政治人物Alckmin評價良好；部分商界人士則認為Fonteles治理能力出色，也可能代表勞工黨內世代交替。黨主席Edinho Silva週一表示，魯拉希望會晤企業領袖，並將以負責任的方式處理財政政策。

制度上的限制也不同於魯拉本屆政府上任之初。盟友不預期再推動容許大幅擴張支出的過渡修憲案，新增支出必須納入更緊的預算。Bolsonaro所屬政黨在先前國會選舉中大幅增加參議院席次，也使魯拉更須與中間派及右派政黨協商。另一方面，Bolsonaro要求撤銷總統選舉結果，指控最高法院臨時延長投票時間改變規則，為經濟重估增添政治不確定性。

## AI企業轉向租賃與股權融資

馬斯克週末宣稱已完成$400億債務融資後，SpaceX週一申報文件釐清晶片融資進度：公司已與Apollo簽訂約$400億設備融資租賃，固定利率將於尚未進行的定價時決定，預計年底前交割，租賃於2027年上半年開始。

高盛擔任唯一架構安排機構。貝萊德及高盛資產管理所管理的基金與帳戶，以及由KKR提供顧問服務的資本帳戶，已作出基石投資承諾。融資架構由表外實體發行私募債券。SpaceX表示，租賃可分散資金來源，支應成長計畫所需資本的相當部分，並稱其AI投資回收期不到一年。

信用市場反應相對有限。ICE Data Services資料顯示，週一早盤違約保障成本約261個基點，略低於週五收盤創紀錄的266個基點。三大評等機構仍給予公司投資等級評等，但保障成本顯示市場對其信用狀況的評價明顯較低。馬斯克強調，Starlink與火箭發射收入，使公司有別於仰賴AI資料中心營收的新型雲端業者。

Meta選擇另一條融資路徑，擬透過普通股與特別股募集最高$950億，以支持AI基礎設施與個人超級智慧。公司表示，輝達、超微及博通合計同意買進最高$50億普通股。這項擬議募資改變大型投資計畫的資金組合，股權需求因而直接關係到債權人原先評估的債券供給與槓桿程度。

Anthropic的IPO申請帶來另一場大型股權融資考驗。這家Claude開發商擬以ANT為代號，在那斯達克全球精選市場掛牌，時程安排在11月3日期中選舉之後，正式推介可能於11月9日當週開始。高盛與摩根士丹利領銜，另有20家銀行參與。募集資金將用於運算、基礎設施，以及招募和留任員工；五類股份架構將使七名共同創辦人掌握50.1%表決權。

文件同時呈現驚人成長與龐大會計虧損。上半年營收由一年前的$12億升至$163億，淨損則由$130億擴大至$807億；淨營收留存率為900%。單看第2季，營收達$116億，營業利益為$9.74億。單季營業獲利與規模大得多的上半年淨損並存，兩者的期間與會計口徑差異，是評估融資需求的關鍵。

大型雲端平台通路對成長的貢獻也提高。亞馬遜、Google與微軟客戶可透過既有帳戶購買Claude，由平台收款、扣留費用後將餘額交給Anthropic。這個通路占2026年上半年營收48%，2023年則為11%。三家公司兼具供應商、投資人、經銷商及競爭者身分，Anthropic的現金創造能力因而與同樣支持基礎設施建設的企業之間的商業關係緊密相連。

Anthropic警告，融資需求可能高於先前預期。不過，DA Davidson的Gil Luria強調公司約有$1,310億現金及約當現金，加上第2季營運表現，認為IPO背後有充足財務儲備。Raymond James分析師Simon Leopold與Jeff Koche則認為，申報內容支持基礎設施支出持續。投資人因此須在龐大資金需求、需求快速成長與既有流動性之間權衡。

公司也揭露，其技術可能帶來災難性及威脅人類存續的風險，且隨系統進一步自動化，風險預期將增加。這些警告與公司仰賴企業客戶的商業模式、AI監管辯論並存。週一股市回升，反映市場重新願意為產業提供資金，但最大幾筆交易的融資條件仍是商業考驗的一部分。

微軟另向美國、加拿大、印度及英國約60,000名員工提出自願離職補償方案，配合以AI為重心的員工結構調整。知情人士表示，部分資料中心、業務與行銷人員不在適用範圍內。公司預期接受比例將遠低於先前針對達退休年齡員工的方案；前次約8,750名符合資格者中，逾30%接受。這使當日募資消息之外，也出現企業調整營運成本的措施。

## 法債反彈，歐洲重新取捨融資方式

穆迪週五維持法國評等後，投資人週一買進法債，帶動相對德國利差出現疫情以來最大單日改善。10年期利差收窄14個基點至154個基點，法國10年期殖利率下降12個基點至4.90%，為4月以來最大降幅。市場未等到新的預算共識，就先部分扭轉前一週的失序惡化。

澳洲退休信託基金（Australian Retirement Trust，ART）則在法債遭到拋售時買進。這家規模A$3,700億的退休基金，9月在法國10年期殖利率超過4.5%時開始買進，10月殖利率升至5%時又加碼。資深投資組合經理Jimmy Louca認為，市場反映的財政惡化過度，也高估歐洲央行緊縮循環的幅度。這些買進屬於基金依自身合理價值估計進行的動態配置。

百達的Christopher Dembik則預期，直到總統大選前，法國10年期殖利率都將介於5%至6%，認為週一改善是技術性反彈，以及評等未變帶來的釋壓。ART預期，高能源成本終將壓縮所得與成長，足以使通膨降溫、殖利率下滑。雙方分歧既涉及法國財政走向，也涉及昂貴能源最終對經濟活動的抑制程度。

週末抗議暴力程度降低，但要求公共支出的壓力仍在。內政部統計全國約410,000人參加，低於前一週的550,000人；CGT工會則估計兩次均約800,000人。學生團體持續要求改善教育經費與大學入學名額。財政部長Roland Lescure提出，可將年度隨通膨調整的最低工資調升提前幾個月；馬克宏則承諾回應合理訴求，同時維持大規模警力部署。

因此，在借款成本仍高之際，近期紓困要求也進入政策辯論。ART買進反映其相信財政終將修復，Dembik則看不到早期解方。週一利差大幅下降，是市場在持續分歧中，對近期評等壓力減輕作出的反應。

英國融資辯論的焦點是期限，而非信用評等。10家主要交易商預估值的中位數顯示，本財政年度國庫券淨發行預期為£110億，高於債務管理局4月預測的£50億。加拿大皇家銀行資本市場預估明年為£250億。政府5月已宣布推出新的12個月期國庫券，預期將配合10月28日預算案說明擴張計畫。

2025年國庫券約占英國借款20%，OECD會員國則約47%。美國銀行的Mark Capleton認為，增加短天期發行可降低平均利息支出，也能透過減少長債供給，緩解長天期英國公債殖利率的壓力。每週國庫券標售需求穩健、銀行持有量增加及貨幣市場基金成長，均支持可能的轉變；但更頻繁再融資也會增加對未來升息的曝險。

另一項政策訊號來自Bloomberg Economics的官員談話分析模型BOESPEAK。貨幣政策委員會成員近期公開談話後，模型達到2023年初以來最鷹派讀數。經濟學家Dan Hanson預期11月及2月升息，同時承認強硬措辭未必轉化為行動。在交易商預期政府將提高短天期借款比重之際，模型也顯示官方措辭轉趨強硬。

## 亞洲信用承壓，主權債表現分歧

中國華發顯示大型國有控股借款人的新一波資金壓力。知情人士表示，這家珠海企業集團自9月起，已要求至少三家中國銀行延長全部貸款期限並降低利率，截至上週仍未談妥條件。另有知情人士表示，兩項近期到期的信託產品也未支付款項。

華發一筆12月到期、票息4.5%的人民幣14億元境外債，稍後報價下跌約9%至面額約89%，為2024年發行以來最大單日跌幅；另一筆2029年到期的人民幣5億元債券，報價下跌12%至約86%。珠海市國資委持有公司約93.5%股權。截至3月，華發申報資產人民幣7,650億元、有息負債4,130億元；去年約一半營收來自房地產開發與城市營運，並錄得人民幣169億元虧損。

美團的融資環境較有利。公司擬發行相當於約$10億的境外人民幣債，預計週二定價，主要用於償還境外人民幣貸款，使原先考慮中的發行更進一步。管理層向投資人表示，將保留較大監管額度的一部分，待條件有利時用於美元再融資；該額度明年9月到期。公司預期2026年資本支出約人民幣200億元，2027年小幅增加。

菲律賓建商Vista Land延後公布的2025年業績，使2027年7月約$4.2億債券到期前的壓力升高。歸屬母公司淨利由76.5億披索下跌約70%至23.3億披索，合併獲利下跌59%至38.3億披索。房地產營收下跌8.7%至151.8億披索，成本則增加約四分之一至190.4億披索。現金與投資減少，主要因償債所致，股東也提供墊款支應到期債務。公司仍表示已達到242億披索的EBITDA目標，目前正尋求融資與出售資產，其中包括兩座潛在價值最高150億披索的購物中心。

巴基斯坦已實際收緊貨幣政策，將基準利率提高50個基點至12%，符合多數受訪經濟學家預期，為4月以來首次升息。央行總裁Jameel Ahmad表示，美國與伊朗衝突、油價高於$100及小麥漲價，使通膨展望明顯惡化。消費者物價通膨已連續七個月超過5%至7%目標區間，決策官員擔心食品與能源漲價擴散至預期及核心通膨。儘管經濟復甦已失去動能，央行仍決定緊縮。

泰國外部融資則呈現不同面貌。外資10月已流入債市$6.04億，有望成為四個月來首次月度淨流入。法國農業信貸銀行預期泰銖於2027年第1季升至每美元32.8，泰京銀行則預期年底前達到該水準，對照上週五的33.76。兩者預測均有賴資金持續流入與觀光收入改善。8月經常帳盈餘$24億，為2月以來最高。

哥倫比亞完成創紀錄的$52億美元債發行，2032、2037及2056年到期債券殖利率分別為7.05%、7.65%及8.15%，均低於初步討論水準，總規模超過1月的$49.5億全球債發行。巴克萊經濟學家Alejandro Arreaza估計今年資金缺口為$30億，其餘款項可能用於預先籌措2027年資金。預算爭議最後以行政命令公布預算收場，總統Abelardo de la Espriella承諾提出財政永續方案。既有美元債當日小幅下跌。

惠譽對南非財政展望提出新的不同看法，預期債務占GDP比重將在約78%停留兩年，之後於2028至2029年度略升至79%，主因是成長疲弱。財政部則預測該比重到2029至2030年度降至76.6%。穆迪採用包含大部分國企擔保的衡量方式，也預期債務比重逐步下降，但警告吸收衝擊的空間有限。兩家機構都將南非評為低於投資等級兩級；惠譽展望穩定，穆迪展望正向。

美國困境債券市場方面，JetBlue預估全年營業利益率將進一步降至更深的負值，為這家背負約$90億債務的借款人再添獲利壓力。公司上次營業獲利是在2019年；債權人先前已聘請重整顧問，這次更新使流動性與營運現金創造能力更為重要。

市場結構另有長期變化。巴克萊估計，採用AI可使投資等級債電子交易量占比由45%升至65%，高收益債占比則倍增至50%。目前應用集中在資訊蒐集、契約條款分析及交易前決策。匯豐的Michael Roberts預期，隨交易執行應用擴大，人員仍將參與；巴克萊則指出，模型同步行動可能引發間歇性波動。澳洲證券投資委員會委員Simone Constant週一也警告，市場條件變化可能削弱流動性，尤其是私募資產，同時明確表示不將目前情況定性為金融危機，也未必是壓力事件。

## 後續市場關注

10月28日聯準會決策前，美國已公布兩項較強的經濟活動數據，殖利率曲線也進一步趨平。市場共識預期政策利率維持4%，決策於UTC 18:00公布，記者會於18:30舉行。焦點是主席Kevin Warsh如何在9月升息後的耐心與持續通膨壓力間取得平衡。Santander的Stephen Stanley預期12月再升息，美國銀行的Aditya Bhave預測10月意外升息，Bloomberg Economics的Anna Wong則預期今年不再升息。若有反對票，委員觀點分布將與主席措辭同樣重要。

週二數據將在決策前擴大經濟活動的觀察範圍。9月耐久財訂單預期增加1.5%，前值持平；不含運輸訂單預期增加0.6%，前值0.3%；不含飛機的非國防訂單預期增加0.7%，前值1.6%。每週ADP就業數據前值增加18,500人。經濟諮商理事會消費者信心指數預估81，前值81.9；新屋銷售預估650,000戶，前值684,000戶。這些數據將檢驗週一全國與區域指標的改善，是否延伸至投資、勞動市場與家庭需求。財政部週二也將標售5年期公債，週四接著標售7年期。

週四公布的第3季GDP初估預期成長3.2%，前值2.2%。9月核心PCE預期月增0.3%、年增3.1%，前值分別為0.2%與3%；整體PCE預期月增0.5%、年增3.6%。所得預期增加0.3%，支出增加0.5%。週五第3季就業成本指數共識為0.8%，前值0.9%。這些數據均在聯準會決策後公布，將有助判斷暫停升息能維持多久。

Alphabet與微軟週三公布財報，亞馬遜與英特爾週四接續。其支出承諾、現金創造能力及部署時程，將為週一大型融資計畫提供營運面的對照。SpaceX仍須為租賃融資定價，Meta須確認擬議股權發行的需求，Anthropic可能在11月進行的推介則將考驗公開市場投資人吸收另一家大型AI發行人的能力。

英國週三預算案將揭示，預期擴大的國庫券融資究竟使借款組合改變多少。歐洲央行週四開會，經濟學家預期存款利率維持2.5%，之後週五公布歐元區成長與通膨。Bloomberg調查預期第3季成長0.2%，前季0.6%。法國財政協商與預定11月5日的罷工，在週一利差回落後，仍是各自獨立的不確定來源。

澳洲第3季通膨、泰國週三利率決策，以及日本週五的日本央行決策與東京CPI，將使全球政策考驗持續。巴西方面，財政部長任命與具體財政方案，是重新評估選舉衝擊的近期條件。美國11月3日投票則帶來另一種前瞻風險：Bloomberg Markets Pulse於10月2日至17日訪問301人，逾半預期若民主黨橫掃兩院，美債殖利率將在隨後一年下降；若共和黨掌控兩院，持此看法的比例為26%。現行舉債授權預計明年下半年到期，近半受訪者認為，若明年債務上限爭議長期延宕，最大影響是美債殖利率上升。

overall_summary.headline: 經濟活動轉強、AI反彈推升短端殖利率，美債曲線趨平；巴西遭遇財政衝擊
overall_summary.session_narrative:
聯準會決策前，AI帶動股市回升，加上美國經濟活動數據優於預期，推升短天期殖利率，美債曲線趨平。2年期上升3.41個基點至4.7159%，10年期下降0.61個基點至4.9884%，30年期下降1.93個基點至5.3028%。2年與10年期利差收窄4.02個基點至27.25個基點。10年期殖利率下降，來自實質殖利率下滑0.36個基點與損益兩平通膨率下降0.25個基點；過去一週及一個月的漲勢仍主要由實質殖利率下降帶動。芝加哥全國活動指標與達拉斯製造業數據均優於預期，支持市場重估近期政策，而非全面撤出公債。

巴西調整猛烈得多。魯拉意外連任，打亂原先押注Bolsonaro將實施財政撙節的部位，部分較長天期交換利率上升逾300個基點，雷亞爾一度貶值11%，美元債表現落後其他新興市場。財政部宣布買回債券後，交換利率略為回穩，下一任財政部長與財政方案仍是展望關鍵。穆迪維持法國評等後，法國10年期相對德國利差收窄14個基點，但財政協商仍未解決。

AI融資另為科技股帶來催化劑。SpaceX與Apollo簽訂約$400億設備融資租賃，仍待定價與交割；Meta尋求最高$950億股權資金；Anthropic在營收快速成長、融資需求持續之際申請IPO。反彈恢復了部分為大規模建設提供資金的意願，營運現金創造能力及各筆交易條件則仍待檢驗。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries flattened as a recovery in artificial-intelligence shares lifted shorter yields while longer debt held its ground ahead of the Federal Reserve decision. The two-year yield rose 3.41 basis points to 4.7159%, but the 10-year edged down 0.61 basis point to 4.9884% and the 30-year fell 1.93 basis points to 5.3028%. Stronger-than-expected U.S. activity readings accompanied the split, leaving the session closer to a reassessment of policy-sensitive maturities than a broad retreat from government bonds.

The more violent adjustment was in Brazil. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise re-election overturned positioning for a government investors expected to deliver tougher fiscal restraint. Longer-dated interest-rate swaps jumped more than 300 basis points at some maturities, the real fell as much as 11%, and dollar bonds underperformed emerging-market peers. France moved the other way: its 10-year premium over Germany narrowed 14 basis points as investors traded the reprieve from Moody's decision to maintain its rating.

AI financing supplied a separate change in the global credit story. SpaceX confirmed a roughly $40 billion equipment-finance lease with Apollo, although pricing and closing remain ahead. Meta sought as much as $95 billion of equity capital, while Anthropic filed for an IPO and disclosed both rapid revenue growth and continuing financing needs. Those developments helped revive technology equities without removing the question confronting creditors: how much of the buildout can be funded by operating cash, and on what terms the remainder can be financed.

## Treasury Curve Flattens as Activity Holds Up

Monday's Treasury adjustment was concentrated at the shorter end. Five-year yields increased 1.95 basis points to 4.8262%, joining the two-year selloff while the 10- and 30-year sectors advanced. The 2s10s spread narrowed 4.02 basis points to 27.25 basis points, and the gap between two and 30 years contracted 5.34 basis points to 58.69 basis points. Long-term borrowing costs were still high, but they resisted the improvement in equity sentiment more successfully than maturities closely exposed to the next policy decisions.

The longer comparison continued to favor duration. Ten-year yields were 15.13 basis points lower than a week earlier and 17.46 basis points below their month-earlier level; the corresponding declines at 30 years were 16.45 and 19.12 basis points. Two-year yields were down only 5.6 basis points over the week, although their monthly decline was 13.81 basis points. Monday extended the weekly flattening even as it gave back some of the front end's recent gains.

At 10 years, the small nominal yield decline reflected modest changes in both components. The real yield slipped 0.36 basis point to 2.6379%, and breakeven inflation declined 0.25 basis point to 2.3505%. Over the week, the real yield had fallen 14.51 basis points while the breakeven was only 0.62 basis point lower. Over the month, real yields were down 18.61 basis points even as inflation compensation rose 1.15 basis points. The larger sustained movement remained a reduction in real yields, with little accompanying retreat in longer-run inflation compensation.

Fresh economic data showed firmer activity ahead of the Fed decision. September's Chicago Fed National Activity Index rose to 0.07 from a revised minus 0.08, exceeding the minus 0.1 forecast. October's Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index increased to 13.4 from 9.8, also above the forecast of 7. The national measure and the regional manufacturing reading were separate improvements, rather than additional evidence of the weakening growth investors had feared during the technology correction.

Treasury's two-year note auction cleared at 4.708%, compared with 4.787% at the previous sale. The lower auction yield put the government's new short-maturity financing cost below the level at the previous sale even though the secondary-market two-year yield rose Monday. The auction and the daily market move describe different comparisons.

Stocks recovered more decisively than bonds moved. The S&P 500 gained 0.70% to 7,676.77, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.09%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index advanced 2.82%. The VIX fell 5.45% to 18.39. Semiconductor shares nevertheless remained down 12.51% over the month, while the Nasdaq 100 was 4.36% lower. The rebound followed a substantial reassessment of AI financing and spending, leaving investors with better daily prices but a much weaker recent technology trend.

Richard Saperstein at Treasury Partners expected the Fed to hold rates because the bond market had already tightened credit conditions since September. Seema Shah at Principal Asset Management likewise saw policymakers responding principally to energy inflation and currency dynamics rather than a materially overheating economy; she expected an increase in December and another in 2027. The stronger activity releases make the distinction consequential: market restraint can support patience without requiring a contemporaneous collapse in measured output.

Energy remained an inflation risk even as oil prices eased. WTI crude futures fell 1.46% to $101.76 a barrel, while Brent crude futures declined 0.78% to $115.81. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for deeper regional cooperation and resolving differences during talks in Tehran with security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, according to state-run IRIB. Their visit sought to revive diplomacy after President Donald Trump said over the weekend that a decision on a deal or renewed attacks was approaching. The oil retreat eased one pressure on the day's markets, while the diplomatic outcome remained open.

Gold futures rose 0.76% to $4,038.40 an ounce.

The Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 102.017. In credit, broad U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly, contrasting with clearly wider hard-currency emerging-market spreads. Investment-grade fund LQD returned about 0.15% and high-yield fund HYG about 0.17%, while emerging-market debt fund EMB lost about 0.17%. The division was consistent with a session in which a U.S. technology recovery coexisted with a major sovereign shock in Latin America.

## Brazil's Election Reprices Fiscal Risk

Lula won 51.8% of the presidential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2%, according to Brazil's electoral court. Investors had largely positioned for Bolsonaro after his first-round lead encouraged expectations of spending cuts and lower interest rates. The result instead returned Lula for a fourth term, forcing an abrupt reassessment of the fiscal adjustment likely to accompany the next government.

The market reaction was amplified by that positioning. The Ibovespa fell 10% at the open, immediately triggering its first circuit breaker since early 2020, and subsequently dropped as much as 17%. The real's decline reached 11% at one point, its steepest in more than two decades. Some longer-dated swap contracts surged more than 300 basis points after reaching trading limits. Exchange operator B3 widened the limits for currency, interest-rate and stock-index futures for Monday's regular session.

Brazil's Treasury announced an auction to buy back local fixed-rate notes, after which swap rates steadied modestly. Dollar bonds still fell across maturities, with some losing more than 2.6 cents and the country underperforming other emerging-market sovereigns. The benchmark for small-cap stocks, which are particularly sensitive to domestic rates, dropped 30%, while a U.S.-listed Brazilian equity fund lost as much as 26% intraday. These were simultaneous shocks to the currency, domestic discount rates and external credit, rather than an equity-only response to the election.

The fiscal concern is the scale and composition of the adjustment. Brazil's nominal deficit exceeds 9% of GDP and public debt is above 80%, while mandatory expenditure leaves limited budget flexibility. Lula has emphasized maintaining social benefits and supporting consumption through credit, with revenue increases doing much of the work in repairing public finances. His campaign included debt relief for microentrepreneurs and accelerated welfare payments, reinforcing doubts about the pace at which expenditure could be restrained.

Lula's stated objective is a primary surplus, excluding interest, of 1.5% of GDP by the end of the next term. Investors interviewed by Bloomberg regarded that as insufficient. The distinction between the primary target and the much larger overall deficit matters because high interest costs remain a heavy claim on the budget. Vanguard's Ales Koutny expected continued fiscal spending, more public investment and inflation staying higher for longer to leave limited room for rate cuts and require elevated real rates.

The financing consequences extended beyond traded securities. About $6 billion of equity offerings lined up for after the vote were thrown into uncertainty, Bloomberg reported. Those transactions had been prepared around an expected Bolsonaro victory. The fall in asset prices therefore also affected companies' prospective access to fresh capital, at a time when expensive borrowing and record household delinquencies were already weighing on the economy.

JPMorgan lowered its assessments of Brazil's currency and rates to market-weight from overweight, and Bradesco BBI cut its stock-market outlook to neutral. Win Thin at Bank of Nassau 1982 attributed part of the outsized moves to positioning and possible overshooting, while judging that Lula's campaign spending promises had worsened the fundamental outlook. Wells Fargo's Alvaro Vivanco considered the immediate reaction excessive and expected sufficient early fiscal measures to contain risks, particularly for the currency. He saw the real strengthening toward 5.30 per dollar under a Lula government.

The next finance minister will help determine which view gains support. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Piauí Governor Rafael Fonteles were among the names being discussed, according to government officials. Alckmin is viewed favorably in market circles as a centrist veteran; some business figures regard Fonteles as a capable governor and a potential generational change within the Workers' Party. Party leader Edinho Silva said Monday that Lula wanted to meet business leaders and would act responsibly on fiscal policy.

The institutional constraints also differ from the start of Lula's current administration. Allies did not expect another large transition amendment permitting a broad expenditure expansion; additional spending would have to fit a tighter budget. Bolsonaro's party made substantial Senate gains in the earlier congressional elections, giving Lula a further reason to negotiate with centrist and right-wing parties. Bolsonaro meanwhile sought annulment of the presidential result, alleging that the Supreme Court's last-minute extension of voting hours changed the rules. That challenge added political uncertainty to the economic repricing.

## AI Borrowers Turn to Leases and Equity

SpaceX's Monday filing clarified the status of its chip financing after Musk's weekend claim that $40 billion of debt had closed. The company signed a roughly $40 billion equipment-finance lease with Apollo, but said the fixed rate would be determined at pricing, which had not yet occurred. Closing is expected before year-end, with the leases starting in the first half of 2027. The new development was a signed agreement with explicit remaining steps and a timetable for using the financed equipment.

Goldman Sachs served as sole structuring agent. Funds and accounts managed by BlackRock and Goldman Sachs Asset Management, together with capital accounts advised by KKR, made anchor commitments. The arrangement is structured around private bonds issued by an off-balance-sheet entity. SpaceX said the lease diversified its funding and covered a substantial portion of the capital required for its growth plans, while claiming payback periods of less than a year on its AI investments.

Its credit market response was restrained. Default-protection costs traded around 261 basis points early Monday, according to ICE Data Services, compared with a record 266 at Friday's close. The company retains investment-grade ratings from the three largest agencies, but its insurance cost remained characteristic of a much more heavily discounted credit. Musk emphasized revenue from Starlink and launches as a distinction from neocloud companies dependent on AI data-center revenue.

Meta chose another financing route, seeking up to $95 billion through common and preferred shares to support AI infrastructure and personal superintelligence. Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom agreed to purchase as much as $5 billion of common shares in aggregate, according to the company. The proposed capital raise changes the mix of funding available for a large investment program, making the appetite for equity directly relevant to the debt supply and leverage creditors had been assessing.

Anthropic's IPO filing brought a second major equity test into view. The Claude developer plans to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as ANT, with the listing intended after the November 3 midterm elections and formal marketing potentially beginning the week of November 9. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the transaction, alongside 20 other banks. Proceeds are intended for compute, infrastructure and hiring and retaining employees. A five-class share structure would give the seven co-founders 50.1% of voting power.

The filing presented extraordinary growth alongside large accounting losses. First-half revenue was $16.3 billion, compared with $1.2 billion a year earlier, while the first-half net loss widened to $80.7 billion from $13 billion. Net revenue retention was 900%. In the second quarter alone, sales reached $11.6 billion and operating profit was $974 million. Those period and accounting distinctions are central to the financing assessment: a quarterly operating profit sits alongside a much larger first-half net loss.

Distribution through the largest cloud platforms supplied an increasing share of that growth. Customers of Amazon, Google and Microsoft can buy Claude through existing accounts; the platforms collect the bill, retain a fee and pass the balance to Anthropic. This channel generated 48% of first-half 2026 revenue, compared with 11% in 2023. The three companies are simultaneously suppliers, investors, distributors and competitors, tying Anthropic's cash generation to commercial relationships across the same firms supporting the infrastructure buildout.

Anthropic warned it might need more financing than previously anticipated. DA Davidson's Gil Luria, however, emphasized about $131 billion of cash and equivalents and the second-quarter operating performance, arguing that the IPO was supported by a substantial financial reserve. Raymond James analysts Simon Leopold and Jeff Koche regarded the filing as supportive of continued infrastructure spending. Investors were thus weighing a very large funding requirement against rapid demand growth and existing liquidity, rather than assessing a company with no operating progress.

The company also disclosed catastrophic and existential risks from its technology, with risks expected to grow as systems automate further. Those warnings sit beside the commercial dependence on enterprise customers and the regulatory debate around AI. Monday's equity recovery suggested renewed willingness to fund the sector, but the financing terms of the largest transactions remain part of the commercial test.

Microsoft separately offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees in the U.S., Canada, India and the UK as it reshaped its workforce around AI. Certain data-center, sales and marketing staff are excluded, according to people familiar with the plans. The company expects a much lower acceptance rate than for its earlier retirement-age offer, under which more than 30% of roughly 8,750 eligible employees accepted. The new program adds an operating-cost response to the day's capital-raising announcements.

## France's Rebound Meets Europe's Funding Choices

French bonds delivered their largest daily spread improvement since the pandemic as investors responded to Friday's Moody's rating reprieve. The 10-year premium over Germany fell 14 basis points to 154 basis points on Monday, while France's 10-year yield declined 12 basis points to 4.90%, its biggest fall since April. The move partially reversed the previous week's disorderly deterioration rather than waiting for a new budget settlement.

Australian Retirement Trust disclosed a contrasting response to the selloff. The A$370 billion pension fund began buying 10-year French debt in September above 4.5% and increased purchases during October as yields reached 5%. Senior portfolio manager Jimmy Louca judged that investors had priced too much fiscal deterioration and too extensive an ECB tightening cycle. The buying forms part of a dynamic allocation program based on the fund's estimate of fair value.

That view contrasts with Pictet's Christopher Dembik, who expected French 10-year yields between 5% and 6% until the presidential election. He characterized Monday's improvement as a technical recovery and relief over the unchanged rating. ART instead expects high energy costs eventually to squeeze income and growth enough to cool inflation and lower yields. The disagreement concerns both France's fiscal trajectory and the extent to which expensive energy ultimately restricts activity.

Weekend protests were less violent, but the pressure for public spending continued. The Interior Ministry counted roughly 410,000 participants nationwide, down from 550,000 a week earlier; the CGT union estimated around 800,000 on each occasion. Student groups continued to demand improvements in education funding and university placements. Finance Minister Roland Lescure floated bringing forward the annual inflation-linked minimum-wage increase by a couple of months, while Macron pledged a response to legitimate demands alongside a continuing heavy security presence.

The current policy debate therefore includes demands for near-term relief while borrowing costs remain elevated. ART's purchases reflect confidence that fiscal repair will eventually prevail; Dembik saw no early solution. Monday's large spread decline was a market response to reduced immediate rating pressure within that continuing disagreement.

Britain's financing debate concerned maturity rather than credit ratings. Primary dealers expected net Treasury-bill issuance of £11 billion in the current fiscal year, according to the median of 10 estimates, against the Debt Management Office's April forecast of £5 billion. Royal Bank of Canada Capital Markets projected £25 billion next year. The government is expected to outline expansion plans alongside the October 28 budget after announcing a new 12-month bill in May.

Bills accounted for about 20% of British borrowing in 2025, compared with roughly 47% across OECD members. Bank of America's Mark Capleton argued that shorter-maturity issuance could reduce average interest expense and ease pressure on longer-maturity gilt yields by reducing the supply of those gilts. Robust weekly bill-auction demand, larger bank holdings and growth in money-market funds support the prospective shift. More frequent refinancing would also increase exposure to future rate rises.

A separate Bloomberg Economics communications model, BOESPEAK, reached its most hawkish reading since early 2023 after recent Monetary Policy Committee appearances. Economist Dan Hanson expected increases in November and February, while acknowledging that tough communication need not translate into action. The model finding is a new assessment of official language, alongside the dealers' expectation that debt management will redirect more borrowing toward shorter maturities.

## Asian Credit Strains and Sovereign Divergence

China's Huafa brought fresh evidence of funding pressure at a large state-controlled borrower. The Zhuhai conglomerate has asked at least three Chinese banks since September to extend all their loans and reduce interest rates, people familiar with the discussions said. The banks had not agreed on terms as of last week. Two recently due trust products also went unpaid, according to other people familiar with the matter.

Huafa's 1.4 billion yuan offshore bond, carrying a 4.5% coupon and due in December, was later indicated about 9% lower around 89% of face value, its biggest daily decline since issuance in 2024. A separate 500 million yuan bond due in 2029 had been indicated 12% lower around 86%. Zhuhai's state-assets commission controls about 93.5% of the company, which reported 765 billion yuan of assets and 413 billion yuan of interest-bearing liabilities as of March. Roughly half of last year's revenue came from property development and urban operations, and the company recorded a 16.9 billion yuan loss.

Meituan moved toward new funding on more favorable terrain. It sought the equivalent of about $1 billion through an offshore yuan offering expected to price Tuesday, mainly to refinance offshore yuan loans. Management told investors it would preserve part of its larger regulatory quota for dollar refinancing when conditions were attractive; that quota expires next September. The specified size, imminent pricing and refinancing purpose advance a sale previously under consideration. The company expects capital spending around 20 billion yuan in 2026, increasing modestly in 2027.

Philippine developer Vista Land's delayed 2025 results added pressure before roughly $420 million of bonds mature in July 2027. Parent-attributable net income fell about 70% to 2.33 billion pesos from 7.65 billion, while consolidated profit dropped 59% to 3.83 billion. Real-estate revenue fell 8.7% to 15.18 billion pesos and costs rose about a quarter to 19.04 billion. Cash and investments declined, mainly because of debt service, and shareholders supplied advances for maturing obligations. The firm nevertheless said it met its 24.2 billion peso EBITDA target. It is pursuing financing and asset sales, including two malls potentially worth up to 15 billion pesos.

Pakistan delivered an actual monetary tightening, raising its benchmark 50 basis points to 12%, as most surveyed economists expected. It was the first increase since April. Governor Jameel Ahmad said the inflation outlook had deteriorated significantly because of the U.S.-Iran conflict, oil above $100 and rising wheat prices. Consumer inflation has exceeded the 5%-7% target range for seven months, and policymakers fear food and energy increases spreading into expectations and core inflation. The bank tightened despite a recovery that had already lost momentum.

Thailand offered a different external-funding picture. Foreign investors have put $604 million into its bonds in October, setting up the first monthly inflow in four months. Credit Agricole expects the baht to reach 32.8 per dollar in Q1 2027, while Krung Thai Bank expects that level by year-end, against Friday's 33.76. Their forecasts depend on sustained inflows and improving tourism receipts. August's $2.4 billion current-account surplus was the largest since February.

Colombia completed a record $5.2 billion dollar-bond sale, pricing 2032, 2037 and 2056 maturities at 7.05%, 7.65% and 8.15%, respectively, below initial discussions. The transaction exceeded January's $4.95 billion global sale. Barclays economist Alejandro Arreaza put this year's funding gap at $3 billion, with the rest likely to prefinance 2027. President Abelardo de la Espriella promised a fiscal-sustainability proposal after a budget dispute ended in issuance by decree. Its existing dollar bonds traded slightly lower on the day.

South Africa's fiscal outlook drew a fresh disagreement from Fitch. It expects debt near 78% of GDP for two years before rising modestly to 79% in 2028-29, mainly because of weak growth. That differs from the Treasury's projected decline to 76.6% by 2029-30. Moody's also expects a gradual decline, using a measure that includes most guarantees to state-owned enterprises, while warning of limited room to absorb shocks. Both agencies rate the sovereign two notches below investment grade; Fitch has a stable outlook and Moody's a positive one.

In U.S. distressed credit, JetBlue widened its projected full-year operating-margin loss, adding a new earnings deterioration to a borrower carrying roughly $9 billion of debt. Its last operating profit was in 2019. The update increased the importance of liquidity and operating cash generation after creditors had already engaged restructuring advisers.

Market structure supplied a separate longer-term development. Barclays estimates AI adoption could raise electronic investment-grade bond trading to 65% of volume from 45%, and double high-yield's share to 50%. Current use centers on information gathering, covenant analysis and pre-trade decisions. HSBC's Michael Roberts expects humans to remain involved as execution expands, while Barclays identifies a risk of synchronized models producing episodic volatility. ASIC commissioner Simone Constant likewise warned Monday that changing market conditions could weaken liquidity, particularly in private assets, while explicitly declining to characterize the situation as a financial crisis or necessarily a stress event.

Bloomberg news coverage was incomplete for this edition, limiting the breadth of the market account.

## Forward Market Significance

The October 28 Fed decision arrives after two stronger U.S. activity readings and a curve that has flattened further. Consensus expects the policy rate to remain at 4%, with the decision at 18:00 UTC and the press conference at 18:30 UTC. The question is how Chair Kevin Warsh balances patience after September's increase with continuing inflation pressure. Santander's Stephen Stanley expects another increase in December; Bank of America's Aditya Bhave instead forecasts an October surprise, while Bloomberg Economics' Anna Wong expects no further increase this year. Possible dissents would make the distribution of views important alongside the chair's language.

Tuesday's releases broaden the activity assessment before that decision. September durable-goods orders are expected to rise 1.5% after no change, with orders excluding transportation up 0.6% after 0.3% and non-defense orders excluding aircraft up 0.7% after 1.6%. Weekly ADP employment follows a previous 18,500 increase. Conference Board confidence is expected at 81 after 81.9, and new-home sales at 650,000 after 684,000. These results will test whether the improvement in Monday's national and regional measures extends to investment, labor and household demand. Treasury's five-year auction is also scheduled Tuesday, followed by seven-year notes Thursday.

Thursday's first Q3 GDP estimate is expected to show 3.2% growth after 2.2%. September core PCE is expected to rise 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year, against 0.2% and 3% previously; headline PCE expectations are 0.5% monthly and 3.6% annually. Income is expected up 0.3% and spending up 0.5%. Friday's Q3 Employment Cost Index consensus is 0.8%, after 0.9%. These releases fall after the Fed decision and will help determine how long any pause can last.

Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, followed by Amazon and Intel Thursday. Their spending commitments, cash generation and deployment schedules will place operating evidence beside Monday's large funding plans. SpaceX still needs to price its lease financing, Meta must establish demand for its proposed equity sale, and Anthropic's prospective November marketing will test public investors' capacity to absorb another major AI issuer.

Britain's Wednesday budget will reveal how far the expected expansion of bill financing changes the borrowing mix. The ECB meets Thursday, with economists expecting the deposit rate to remain 2.5%, before Friday's euro-area growth and inflation releases. Bloomberg's growth poll anticipates Q3 expansion of 0.2% after 0.6%. France's fiscal negotiations and planned November 5 strikes remain independent sources of uncertainty after Monday's spread recovery.

Australia's Q3 inflation, Thailand's Wednesday rate decision and Japan's Friday BOJ decision and Tokyo CPI extend the global policy tests. For Brazil, the finance-minister appointment and concrete fiscal program are the immediate conditions for reassessing the election shock. In the U.S., the November 3 vote adds a different prospective risk: a Bloomberg Markets Pulse poll of 301 respondents conducted October 2-17 found more than half expected Treasury yields to fall over the following year after a Democratic sweep, compared with 26% after Republican control of both chambers. Nearly half regarded higher Treasury yields as the largest consequence of a prolonged debt-ceiling fight next year, when current borrowing authority is on course to expire in the second half. Those are distinct conditional judgments about regulation, fiscal policy and financing, with the election outcome still ahead.

The 10-year decline combined a 0.36-basis-point fall in real yield with a 0.25-basis-point drop in breakeven inflation; lower real yields still accounted for most of the weekly and monthly rally. Chicago’s national activity measure and Dallas manufacturing both beat forecasts, supporting a reassessment of near-term policy rather than a broad retreat from government bonds.

Brazil faced a much sharper adjustment after Lula’s surprise re-election overturned positioning for fiscal restraint under Bolsonaro. Longer swaps jumped more than 300 basis points at some maturities, the real fell as much as 11%, and dollar bonds underperformed EM peers. A Treasury buyback announcement steadied swaps modestly, leaving the next finance minister and fiscal program central to the outlook. France’s 10-year premium over Germany narrowed 14 basis points after Moody’s maintained its rating, although fiscal negotiations remained unresolved.

AI financing supplied a separate catalyst for technology shares. SpaceX signed a roughly $40 billion equipment-finance lease with Apollo that still requires pricing and closing; Meta sought up to $95 billion of equity, and Anthropic filed for an IPO amid rapid revenue growth and continuing financing needs. The rebound restored some willingness to fund the buildout, with operating cash generation and the terms of these transactions still to be tested.
